title: PRESIDENT OF INDIA GRACES BALI JATRA FESTIVAL 2026 AT KATAKA
subtitle: DRAW INSPIRATION FROM THE PAST TO SHAPE THE PRESENT AND BRIGHTEN THE FUTURE: PRESIDENT DROUPADI MURMU
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                24 NOV 2026 8:16PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The President of India, Smt Droupadi Murmu graced the Bali Jatra Festival 2026 at Kataka, Odisha today (November 24, 2026).
Speaking on the occasion, the President said that Bali Jatra is a unique festival which celebrates the glorious history of Odisha. The history of maritime trade has evolved into a tradition and the tradition has become a festival. This reflects both the creativity and the historical perspective of the people of Odisha.
The President said that the merchants from Odisha used to travel to distant lands to engage in trade and commerce. Through trade, they accomplished many significant things for the country. They discovered new maritime routes and strengthened international relations. They were also a medium of cultural exchange.
The President said that the historic connection between Odisha and Bali could be transformed into modern commercial and cultural cooperation. She was happy to note that cultural troupes from Indonesia are participating in this Bali Jatra. The Odisha Festival is being celebrated in Bali over two days, featuring Odisha’s dance and music, handlooms, handicrafts, and traditional cuisine. She expressed confidence that such cultural exchanges will strengthen the historic ties between India and Indonesia.
The President said that it is good to be proud of glories of the past and celebrate our festivals. But we should draw inspiration from the past to shape the present and brighten the future. Our younger generation, in particular, has much to learn from the courage and competence of our merchants.
The President said that building Viksit Bharat is our national goal. India’s stature on the international stage has grown. While there is unrest in many parts of the world and instability in the global economy, India’s economy continues to remain strong. This is a promising indicator of our journey toward becoming Viksit Bharat.
The President was happy to note that Odisha is emerging as an industrial hub and is attracting an increasing number of investors. Entrepreneurs, artisans, weavers and the younger generation in Odisha are strengthening the state's economy through their skills and spirit of enterprise. Their growing contributions are an encouraging sign of progress towards realizing the vision of Viksit Odisha.

title: Vice-President Calls for Stronger Global Academic Partnerships to Address Emerging Economic and Social Challenges
subtitle:
Academic Excellence Must Translate into Progress for Society: Vice-President

Today’s Youth Must Lead India and Humanity Towards a Better Future: Vice-President

India’s Development Experience Has Much to Offer the Global Academic Community: Vice-President

Vice-President Graces MoU Exchange Ceremony between London School of Economics, University of Delhi and Institute of Economic Growth
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                24 NOV 2026 5:55PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Vice-President of India and Chancellor of the University of Delhi, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan, today graced the Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) exchange ceremony between the London School of Economics and Political Science (LSE), Delhi School of Economics, University of Delhi, and the Institute of Economic Growth (IEG) at Uprashtrapati Bhavan, New Delhi.
Vice-President of India and Chancellor of the University of Delhi, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan graced the MoU exchange ceremony between the London School of Economics and Political Science (LSE), Delhi School of Economics and the Institute of Economic Growth at Uprashtrapati Bhavan, New Delhi today. 

He described the collaboration as an important milestone that brings together academic excellence, research capabilities and policy expertise to address contemporary economic and social challenges.

The ceremony was attended by Shri N. K. Singh, President, Institute of Economic Growth; Prof. Larry Kramer, President and Vice-Chancellor, London School of Economics and Political Science; Dr. Michael Debabrata Patra, Chairman, Institute of Economic Growth; and Prof. Yogesh Singh, Vice-Chancellor, University of Delhi, among other dignitaries, faculty members and students.

@UnivofDelhi @IEGResearch
— Vice-President of India (@VPIndia)
November 24, 2026
Addressing the gathering, the Vice-President described the collaboration as an important milestone in the journey of the three distinguished institutions. He said that the partnership brings together academic excellence, research capabilities and policy experience to address some of the most pressing economic and social challenges of our times. Recalling the discussions held earlier this year with Shri N. K. Singh on fostering cooperation among these institutions, he expressed satisfaction that the idea had culminated in concrete institutional partnerships.
Emphasising the importance of research and academic excellence, the Vice-President said that universities must strive to strengthen their research capabilities and improve their global standing to provide the best opportunities to India’s youth. He urged students to make full use of the opportunities available to them today and contribute meaningfully to the nation’s development. He observed that the proposed collaboration would facilitate academic exchanges, joint research, training programmes and student-faculty exchanges, opening new avenues for mutual learning and knowledge creation.
The Vice-President particularly welcomed the proposal for a joint research seed fund involving the three institutions. He noted that the identified areas of collaboration, including sustainability, artificial intelligence, public policy, geopolitics and international trade, were highly relevant to contemporary challenges. He expressed hope that the initiative would nurture young researchers, encourage original scholarship and generate practical policy recommendations. He also highlighted the proposed collaboration between IEG and LSE to enhance the training of Indian Economic Service officers, observing that international exposure to research and policy practices would further strengthen their professional capabilities.
Highlighting India’s development journey under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, the Vice-President referred to achievements in poverty alleviation, housing, rural electrification and tap water connectivity. He said that the vision of Viksit Bharat@2047 calls for inclusive development across all sectors, regions and sections of society. Emphasising the importance of wealth creation alongside equitable distribution, he observed that economic progress must ultimately translate into an improved quality of life for people. He also underscored that global and domestic priorities must remain centred on human development, good governance and the welfare of citizens.
Referring to India’s growing role in the Global South, the Vice-President said that India’s democratic institutions, diversity and developmental experience have much to offer the international academic community. He noted that the experiences of developing countries must inform global academic and policy frameworks and that such partnerships can enrich international research and policy discourse.
The Vice-President expressed confidence that the collaboration would transcend institutional boundaries and foster meaningful intellectual exchange. He said that, as Chancellor of the University of Delhi, he would personally monitor the progress and outcomes of this initiative and extend all necessary support. He also encouraged other universities to draw inspiration from this partnership and pursue similar collaborations. He called upon the institutions to translate academic excellence and shared knowledge into tangible progress for society.
The ceremony was attended by Shri N. K. Singh, President, Institute of Economic Growth; Prof. Larry Kramer, President and Vice-Chancellor, London School of Economics and Political Science; Dr. Michael Debabrata Patra, Chairman, Institute of Economic Growth; and Prof. Yogesh Singh, Vice-Chancellor, University of Delhi, among other dignitaries, faculty members and students.

title: India’s Space Economy Set for a Massive Leap to USD 40–45 billion as Private Sector Rewrites Growth Story: Dr. Jitendra Singh
subtitle:
From single-digit startups to 400–500 space companies, India’s space ecosystem witnesses unprecedented expansion following sectoral reforms: Dr. Jitendra Singh at India International Space Conclave 2026

Space reforms under Prime Minister Narendra Modi unlock private investment, entrepreneurship and indigenous technological capabilities, says Dr. Jitendra Singh

PM Gati Shakti has helped improve infrastructure planning, maintain project timelines, reduce costs and minimise wastage and leakages; Space technology has applications across virtually every Ministry: Dr Jitendra Singh

Space technology increasingly powering infrastructure, railways, defence and flagship government programmes beyond satellite launches: Dr. Jitendra Singh

Dr. Jitendra Singh urges industry to scale up investments, support R&D through CSR and strengthen scientific philanthropy
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                24 NOV 2026 5:13PM by PIB Delhi
content:
India's space economy, currently valued at nearly USD 9 billion, is set to grow to USD 40-45 billion in less than a decade, with the private sector driving a major transformation of the country's space ecosystem, Union Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Science & Technology and Earth Sciences, and Minister of State in the Prime Minister's Office, Personnel, Public Grievances and Pensions, Atomic Energy and Space, Dr. Jitendra Singh said today.
Addressing the fifth India International Space Conclave 2026 in New Delhi, the Minister said India's space ecosystem has expanded from single-digit startups to nearly 400-500 companies in just a few years, demonstrating how the reforms initiated under Prime Minister Narendra Modi have unlocked the country's immense entrepreneurial and technological potential.
The two-day conclave, organised by the Indian Space Association (ISpA) on November 23–24, 2026, at New Delhi, was centred on the theme 'Shaping the Future of Space through Innovation, Governance, Human Potential and Global Collaborations'. It brought together industry leaders, space startups, researchers and international stakeholders to deliberate on India's growing role in the global space economy. The occasion also witnessed the launch of the report 'Space Economy 2036: The India Blueprint'.
The programme was attended by Dr. V. Narayanan, Chairman, Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) and Secretary, Department of Space (DoS); Dr. Pawan Kumar Goenka, Chairman, IN-SPACe; Lt Gen Anil Kumar Bhatt (Retd), Director General, Indian Space Association; and Arun T. Ramchandanialong with other prominent representatives of the space industry and technology ecosystem.
Dr. Jitendra Singh said the establishment of New Space India Limited (NSIL), followed by the creation of IN-SPACe and the opening up of the space sector to private participation, marked a decisive transformation in India's space journey. Describing these reforms as among the most transformative policy decisions in recent decades, he said they broke the traditional status quo and enabled private enterprises to participate in a sector that had largely remained within the government domain.
Citing the progress of Indian space startups, the Minister referred to Skyroot's maiden launch vehicle flight on July 18, 2026, its multi-mission launch agreement and unicorn status as significant milestones. He also cited Agnikul and other companies developing advanced propulsion systems, privately built rocket engines, earth-observation technologies and satellite imaging capabilities as evidence of India's growing technological strengths. He said the expanding participation of companies from other industrial sectors further demonstrated the commercial opportunities emerging from the reforms.
The Minister said the economic contribution of space technology must be measured not only through rocket launches, satellite manufacturing and commercial revenues but also through the savings, efficiencies and improved outcomes it generates across sectors on the ground.
Citing the PM Gati Shakti National Master Plan, he said space-based applications help improve infrastructure planning, maintain project timelines, reduce costs and minimise wastage and leakages. He said space technology has applications across virtually every Ministry, including infrastructure, construction, communication, education, healthcare, railways and defence.
During the interactive Q&A session, responding to a question on generating greater demand for the space industry, Dr. Jitendra Singh said the perceived lack of demand was largely linked to insufficient awareness about the practical applications of space technology. He said its potential extended far beyond rocket launches and satellite missions, with significant opportunities in infrastructure, communication and public service delivery. He also cited the Prime Minister's whole-of-government approach and inter-ministerial collaboration as important enablers for expanding the use of space technology across sectors.
Responding to a question on balancing strategic sovereignty with international cooperation, Dr. Jitendra Singh said technological sovereignty and global collaboration were not contradictory. He said India must continue to strengthen indigenous capabilities, with the guiding approach centred on indigenous sources, indigenous technology and indigenous projects, while remaining open to mutually beneficial international partnerships.
The Minister also referred to India's progress under the National Quantum Mission, launched by Prime Minister Narendra Modi in 2023 with an eight-year mandate. He said India had achieved 1,000 kilometres in secure quantum communication in just three years, against the original target of 2,000 kilometres over eight years. He said space, quantum technologies, semiconductors and nuclear science were interconnected areas offering significant opportunities for technological advancement and commercial growth.
Dr. Jitendra Singh urged domestic private players to scale up investments in the space sector and encouraged industry leaders to facilitate greater overseas investment into India's growing space ecosystem. He said the government had introduced enabling mechanisms, including the Anusandhan National Research Foundation and the Research, Development and Innovation (RDI) Fund, to strengthen research and innovation and encourage private-sector participation.
The Minister also urged industry leaders to direct greater Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) support towards research and scientific development. He said CSR should serve the wider community and not remain confined to expenditure on machinery and infrastructure. Calling for a stronger culture of scientific philanthropy, he said investment in research should be regarded as a meaningful contribution to society and humanity.
During the session, he also responded to suggestions on an international space innovation alliance, a global accelerator programme for startups and international grand challenges to encourage innovation. He said India must adopt global strategies and benchmarks to strengthen its international role and that possibilities for institutionalising wider international space cooperation could be explored.
Welcoming suggestions from industry representatives on expanding the space ecosystem to more states and encouraging greater participation of students and young innovators, Dr. Jitendra Singh said the government remained open to constructive feedback and further policy improvements to facilitate private-sector participation.
The Minister said India's space transformation, driven by policy reforms, indigenous technological capabilities and private-sector entrepreneurship, was creating a strong foundation for the country's emergence as a globally competitive space economy.

The Agricultural and Processed Food Products Export Development Authority (APEDA), under the Department of Commerce, Ministry of Commerce and Industry, Government of India, organised an ‘Interaction with Stakeholders’ programme on 20 November 2026 in Varanasi.

Farrukhabad and its adjoining areas have considerable potential for vegetable production and processing. He further highlighted APEDA's BHARATI initiative, which seeks to empower FPOs and facilitate their integration into export value chains, enabling them to access international markets.

Through stakeholder engagement, market development initiatives, infrastructure support and capacity-building programmes, APEDA continues to facilitate the expansion of India's agricultural and processed food exports. subtitle:
Over the last decade, India has moved from being the consumer of technology to becoming the creator of technology, Telecom sector being the most profound example of it: Shri Jyotiraditya M. Scindia

Conclave brings together startups, MSMEs, investors and industry leaders to accelerate development and commercialisation of indigenous telecom technologies

DoT Reaffirms Commitment to Strengthening Indigenous Telecom Innovation and Entrepreneurship
date:

content:
Union Minister for Communications and Development of North Eastern Region Shri Jyotiraditya M. Scindia today chaired the Telecom Startups and MSME Conclave 2026, organised by the Department of Telecommunications (DoT), Ministry of Communications, at Leaders Lounge, Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi. The Conclave underscored the Government's commitment to strengthening indigenous telecom innovation, promoting entrepreneurship and facilitating the development and commercialisation of homegrown technologies.
The Conclave brought together telecom startups, Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs), industry leaders, investors, academia and government representatives on a common platform to showcase indigenous products and solutions, deliberate on challenges faced by domestic innovators and explore opportunities for scaling up Indian telecom technologies.
Ms. Debjani Ghosh, Distinguished Fellow at NITI Aayog and Chief Architect of the NITI Frontier Tech Hub, delivered the keynote address during the session, highlighting the importance of fostering innovation, strengthening collaboration among stakeholders and creating an enabling ecosystem for technology-led entrepreneurship.
The Conclave featured presentations and discussions across five key thematic areas covering the telecom technology stack, namely Radio Access Network (RAN) and Core, Applications, Chipsets, Security and Standards. Each thematic group was represented by the concerned DoT officials, who apprised participants of various Government initiatives, policy interventions and enabling frameworks being undertaken by the Department to support startups and MSMEs and strengthen the overall telecom innovation ecosystem. The Conclave also featured 11 exhibition stalls set up by startups and MSMEs, providing them an opportunity to showcase their innovative indigenous products, technologies and solutions to policymakers, industry leaders, investors and other stakeholders.
The Union Minister also felicitated the winners of the Emerging Technologies Hackathon 2026 (ETH 2026), organised by TCoE India. The Hackathon received over 2,870 registrations and 620 applications across nine technology domains, with participation from students, startups, companies and academic institutions. The winners were recognised with awards and prize money for their innovative solutions. Entra Innovations LLP secured the
First Prize
for
VAAYU
, an indigenously designed tyre-pressure sensor system-on-chip; Dawniens International Private Limited received the
Second Prize
for
Cablesmith
, a robotic optical patch panel solution enabling remote provisioning of fibre connections; while the
Joint Third Prize
was awarded to IIT Bombay (Team DRISTI) for
KAVACH
, a security engine for private 5G networks, and the Military College of Telecommunication Engineering (Team RUDRA) for
VajraLink
, an anti-jamming communication solution for drones.
Speaking during the conclave, the Union Minister said,
“
Today has been an exhilarating experience in terms of the re-emergence of India’s entrepreneurial strength in the past decade. Our country has always been the home of innovation, technology, science and entrepreneurship. For thousands of years, India has contributed in the advancement of mankind. Over the last decade, India has moved from being the consumer of technology to becoming the creator of technology. Under the leadership of Hon’ble Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, today India has risen as the 4th largest economy and market in the world. From a country that had only few hundred startups in 2014, India has now gone beyond 2,00,000 startups and this has happened because of multiple prompt approaches by the Hon’ble Prime Minister.”
He also added that,
“
The telecom sector is the most profound example of India becoming the creator of technology due to the volume to test technology. From a country that only had 25 crore internet connections to now 110 crore internet connections, from 6 crore broadband connections to 104 crore broadband connections. We are the only telecom network market in the world that is growing at double digit numbers.”
The Department of Telecommunications (DoT) is implementing various initiatives to strengthen the indigenous telecom innovation ecosystem, including the
Telecom Technology Development Fund (TTDF)
,
Technology Development and Investment Promotion (TDIP) Scheme
and
100 5G Use Case Labs
, which support research and development, global standardisation, product validation and deployment. Complementing these initiatives, the
Telecommunications Act, 2023
, through the frameworks for Captive Non-Public Networks (CNPNs) and Regulatory Sandbox, provides an enabling policy environment for enterprise networks and live testing of innovative telecom technologies.
In this context, the Conclave featured dedicated sessions on
Captive Telecommunication Services
and
Regulatory Sandbox
, wherein DoT representatives apprised participants of the relevant regulatory frameworks and their provisions. Ericsson shared global perspectives and industry experiences on both subjects. The sessions also provided a platform for interaction among user agencies, industry representatives, startups and other stakeholders to exchange views on potential applications, implementation requirements and opportunities arising from these frameworks.
The Conclave reaffirmed DoT's commitment to fostering collaboration among startups, MSMEs, academia, investors and industry, strengthening indigenous technological capabilities and creating an enabling environment for innovation and entrepreneurship, in alignment with the vision of
Viksit Bharat@2047
.

Established in 1952, the Indian Society of Aerospace Medicine (ISAM) stands as the nation's sole registered aeromedical society. Dedicated to fostering the exchange of knowledge and pioneering research to resolve complex aeromedical challenges, the Society has convened its annual scientific conference since 1954. This year, ISAM will host its 65th Annual Conference from 26-27 November 2026 at the Institute of Aerospace Medicine (IAM), Bengaluru. As the premier nodal hub for aeromedical activities in India, IAM plays a critical role in providing medical support for the design and development of indigenous aircraft and India's ambitious human spaceflight programme. The theme for this year, 'One Airspace - One Mission: Aeromedical Support from Runway to Orbit', articulates a unified vision of Aerospace Medicine that seamlessly integrates military aviation, civil aviation and human spaceflight. This theme underscores the synergy between clinical excellence, operational medicine, and cutting-edge research, aimed at harmonising standards and enhancing interdisciplinary collaboration across every domain of flight.
The conference will be inaugurated by Air Chief Marshal Ashutosh Dixit, Chief of the Air Staff (CAS), in the presence of distinguished military and civil dignitaries from India and abroad. The event expects to draw approximately 250 delegates, including medical professionals from the military and civil aviation sectors, IAF aircrew and eminent scientists from DRDO, the aerospace industry agencies.
A key highlight of the event will be the Air Marshal Subroto Mukerjee Memorial Oration, to be delivered by Shri APVS Prasad, Chief Executive, CEMILAC, Air Vice Marshal Srinagesh Memorial Oration will be delivered by Air Vice Marshal Anupam Agarwal (Retd), Principal Consultant (Aerospace Medicine), Airport Authority of India. Furthermore, the JHF Manekshaw Panel will feature expert insights from Wing Commander Surender Sodhi (Retd) and Colonel KN Rao (Retd). In a landmark addition this year, the Society is launching a premier lecture series the "Cosmonaut Rakesh Sharma lecture" to honour the monumental legacy of Cosmonaut Wing Commander Rakesh Sharma (Retd). This series aims to unite visionaries and trailblazers to deliberate on the future of space exploration and India's expanding footprint in Space Medicine and technology. The inaugural lecture will be delivered by Mr Pawan Kumar Chandana, CEO, Skyroot Aerospace.
The scientific programme will feature over 100 research papers presented through panels, symposia, podiums and poster sessions. Complementing the deliberations, a scientific exhibition will showcase state-of-the-art aeromedical equipment and biomedical devices. The conference will serve as a forum for intellectual exchange, providing a unique opportunity for subject matter experts to collaborate and roster jointness in the advancement of aerospace medicine.

The celebration will provide an important platform to recognise the contributions of dairy farmers and stakeholders, showcase key developments and initiatives, and promote greater collaboration towards building a robust, inclusive and globally competitive livestock and dairy ecosystem.
National Milk Day commemorates the birth anniversary of Dr. Verghese Kurien, the Father of the White Revolution in India, and recognises his invaluable contribution to transforming India into the world's largest milk producer. title: “Celebrate Cinema by Bringing People Together”: Gujarati Film, Laalo – Krishna Sada Sahaayate wins hearts at IFFI 2026

Laalo – Krishna Sada Sahaayate
, a 2025 Gujarati spiritual drama directed by Ankit Bhupatbhai Sakhiya featured in the Indian Panorama section at the 57th International Film Festival of India (IFFI) 2026 in Goa today. The film follows a struggling rickshaw driver with a troubled past and a life of poverty, who is trapped in a remote farmhouse, where he confronts his guilt and seeks redemption through visions of Lord Krishna. At its heart, the film celebrates faith and resilience. Lord Krishna serves as a silent companion to the protagonist, guiding his journey of self-reflection and healing. The director said his intention was to create an emotional connection with audiences through the universal themes of love, faith and inner transformation.
Explaining the title, Sakhiya said ‘Laalo’ is an affectionate name for Lord Krishna, also used for little boys. Marking Sakhiya’s debut as a feature-film director, the film was made on a modest budget, with financial support from friends who also became part of the cast.
Sakhiya recalled that the film gradually gained popularity through word of mouth and went on to register a reported box-office collection of around Rs. 130 crores. He credited social media for expanding its reach through videos capturing audience reactions. He also recalled the special experience of screening the film in his own village and receiving the affection and blessings of its people.
Speaking about its creative approach, Sakhiya highlighted the influence of Garba on the film's music and the use of close-up shots to convey emotions. The music director contributed remotely from Australia. The film relies on natural performances, dialogue and emotional depth rather than visual grandeur. The film is simple and mostly shot in a linear form, yet Sakhiya wanted it to engage the audience. The story also evolved organically.
On the future of Gujarati cinema, Sakhiya said the state's rich cultural heritage offers many stories waiting to be told. He expressed optimism about the growing presence of regional cinema and emphasised the need to prioritise meaningful storytelling alongside commercial success.

title: Elephants in the Fog Explores the Paradox of Social Acceptance and Exclusion: Director Abinash Bikram Shah
subtitle: Director Uses Elephant Metaphor to Examine Social Prejudice in Elephants in the Fog
content:
Goa, 24 November 2026
A society that welcomes transgender women during auspicious occasions but often denies them dignity and acceptance in everyday life forms the central paradox explored in Nepali feature film
Elephants in the Fog
. Director and screenwriter Abinash Bikram Shah and lead actor Pushpa Thing Lama discussed the film and its themes during a press interaction organized on the sidelines of the 57th International Film Festival of India (IFFI) in Goa.
The film, which received the Jury Prize in the
Un Certain Regard
section and the
Best Sound Creation Award
at the 79th Cannes Film Festival, now marks another significant milestone for Nepali cinema on the international stage.
Set in Nepal,
Elephants in the Fog
follows Pirati, a transgender woman and mother of three daughters, who dreams of building a new life with the man she loves. Her aspirations are disrupted when her youngest daughter, Apsara, goes missing during a night patrol organised to protect the village from wild elephants. As the search unfolds, the film examines the intersections of motherhood, identity, personal freedom and social exclusion.
Sharing the film’s journey to Cannes, Shah described the international recognition as surreal and expressed satisfaction at representing Nepali cinema on a global platform. He said receiving two awards was particularly gratifying, noting that the
Best Sound Creation Award
held special significance for a film seeking to amplify voices and experiences that often remain unheard.
Explaining the title, Shah said elephants were not part of the original screenplay but gradually emerged as a metaphor for the film’s central theme. He drew a parallel between elephants, revered when within accepted boundaries but feared when they cross them, and transgender people, welcomed during auspicious occasions but often denied dignity and acceptance in everyday life. Through this contrast, the film questions society’s conditional acceptance of marginalized communities.
For Pushpa Thing Lama, portraying Pirati was both a challenging and deeply personal experience. Speaking from her own perspective as a transgender woman, she highlighted the difficulties transgender people continue to face in securing social acceptance and recognition. She described the film as an opportunity to bring their experiences to a wider audience and enable their stories to be seen, heard and understood.
Reflecting on her preparation for the role, Lama said it required her to draw upon real-life experiences and emotions and understand the character’s journey from within. She also spoke about the influence of her mother’s upbringing and teachings in shaping her outlook towards life, resilience and the challenges of confronting society.
The filmmaker said the film took nearly three years to develop. Through Pirati’s journey and the metaphor of elephants,
Elephants in the Fog
examines social boundaries around identity and belonging, highlighting the gap between symbolic acceptance and the everyday denial of dignity.
The press interaction was moderated by Lekshmi Priya.

title: Mid-fest film ‘I Matter’ Explores Identity, Belonging and the Many Layers of Humanity: Director Alina Șerban at IFFI 2026
subtitle: Working on the lead character helped me embrace my Roma roots with pride: Lead Actress Denisa Farcaș
content:
Goa, 24 November 2026
There are many untold stories from the Roma community waiting to be discovered, said Romanian-Roma filmmaker Alina Șerban, director of
I Matter
(
Eu Contez
), the Mid-Fest film at the 57th International Film Festival of India (IFFI) in Goa.
Interacting with the media at a press conference organised by the Press Information Bureau (PIB) on the sidelines of IFFI today, Șerban spoke about the inspiration behind the film, its portrayal of the Roma community and the importance of challenging stereotypes through cinema. Lead actresses Denisa Farcaș and Vanessa Dancea also participated in the interaction.
A multilingual drama featuring dialogues in Romanian and Romani,
I Matter
had its Indian premiere at IFFI today. A co-production of Romania, Germany and Belgium, the film explores identity, family, belonging and the pursuit of a future beyond one's past. It follows Rebeca, a young Roma woman preparing to leave the orphanage she has called home. As she hopes to reunite with her father, who is about to be released from prison, and build the family she has always longed for, her admission to university to study acting offers the possibility of a new beginning.
Responding to a question on challenging stereotypes through cinema, she said the film seeks to explore different dimensions of humanity. “
The film asks questions about who deserves to be a human. I want to portray different layers of humanity
,” she said. She also expressed happiness at being part of IFFI, describing her visit to India as a homecoming.
Highlighting the challenges of representing the Roma community on screen, Șerban observed that despite its significant cultural influence, the community continues to remain on the margins of society. “
Our culture, like flamenco, has impacted universal culture. But we are still at the margins of society. We live so close to other people, but they still don't know us
,” she said.
Emphasising the film's message of empowerment, Șerban said she wanted to reach out particularly to young people from disadvantaged backgrounds. “
I wanted to tell a story that would empower, first and foremost, young people from disadvantaged groups. I wanted to tell them what I also needed to hear: that I will manage, that there is maybe a small place for each of us in the world
,” she said.
Lead actress Denisa Farcaș, who portrays Rebeca, described the film as a deeply personal experience that transformed her relationship with her own identity. Recalling her initial hesitation about acknowledging her Roma ethnicity, she said, “For the first time, I saw Roma people in a positive light.” She added that portraying the character helped her overcome the shame associated with her identity and embrace her roots with pride. “I am proud to be Roma,” she said, expressing happiness that the stories of the community and its children were finally being heard.
The session was moderated by Pranjal Rai.

title: “Not Only Filmmakers, Every Human Being Breathes Stories”: Bogdan Mureșanu at IFFI Masterclass
subtitle: “When a Monologue in your Mind Becomes a Dialogue, the Film Is No Longer Yours Alone”: Mureșanu
content:
Goa, 24 November 2026
Every story carries a fragment of reality, just as every memory holds the possibility of fiction. Exploring this intricate space between lived experience and cinematic imagination, acclaimed Romanian writer-director and producer Bogdan Mureșanu conducted an engaging masterclass titled
‘The Thin Borders Between the Reality and Fiction’
at the 57th International Film Festival of India (IFFI) in Goa today.
Addressing an enthusiastic gathering of cinephiles, students and film professionals, Mureșanu shared insightful reflections on why storytelling is intrinsic to human existence and how narratives help us comprehend the world. Emphasising that storytelling is not the exclusive domain of artists, he observed that from everyday anecdotes shared among friends to stories told through cinema, narratives allow us to explore possible realities and recharge our spirit.
He described filmmaking as a deeply personal process that ultimately transforms into a collective experience. “When a monologue in your mind becomes a dialogue, the film is no longer yours alone,” he remarked, highlighting how a filmmaker's private vision finds new meaning through the audience's interpretation. Discussing the craft of cinema, Mureșanu emphasised the importance of a clear central idea. “Unlike a novel, which can accommodate several narrative diversions, a two-hour film must remain focused, with its context, premise and themes aligned with a strong central vision”, he asserted.
He also highlighted the power of the ‘unspoken’ in cinematic storytelling. Recalling a sequence in one of his films, he explained how he deliberately chose not to show a character lighting a firecracker, leaving the moment to the audience's imagination. Such creative restraint, he noted, allows viewers to emotionally participate in the story.
Challenging the perception of archival footage as an entirely objective representation of history, Mureșanu pointed out that every camera captures only one perspective. Drawing on his films
The Christmas Gift
and
The New Year That Never Came
, he discussed how archival material and fictional narratives can complement one another. Sharing a fascinating anecdote, he observed, “When fiction works as a simplified model to understand reality, it becomes one with reality. They feed each other.”
Mureșanu further explored how visual language shapes storytelling, explaining his use of the 4:3 aspect ratio in films set during Romania's communist era to complement archival footage and create a sense of intimacy and confinement. In contrast, his animated short
The Magician
, employed a sweeping widescreen format that gave the harbour an active narrative presence.
Reflecting on contemporary cinema, he stressed that true cinematic power lies not merely in pace or spectacle, but in the expressive possibilities of the human face and the emotions conveyed through a gaze. The interactive Q&A explored historical biopics, mythology and the ethical responsibilities of portraying real-life personalities. Referring to a recent offer to direct a biopic on legendary personality, Mureșanu observed that focusing on a defining chapter of a person's life can often reveal deeper truths than attempting an exhaustive biography.
Concluding on a philosophical note, he encouraged storytellers to move beyond inherited perspectives, engage with the wider world and return to their roots with courage and clarity.

Speaking at a Press Conference organised by Press Information Bureau today, actress Amala Paul said that roles involving vampires and supernatural characters are rarely offered to actors, making
Half
a particularly exciting project for her. She described it as an opportunity to step into a character she had never imagined portraying, something she had always wanted to explore as an actor.
Actor Abbas described his role in the film as something distinctly different from his previous projects. Recalling the challenges of filming in the intense heat of Jaisalmer, he said the experience pushed him beyond familiar territory. Describing the film as a surprise package, he praised the entire team for their efforts in creating an entertaining cinematic experience for audiences.
For actor Ranjith Sajeev, his passion for acting made the project particularly exciting. Describing
Half
as an action thriller with a distinctive approach, he revealed that both lead actors, himself and
Aiswarya Raj, underwent an intensive workshop to prepare for the demanding action sequences. Explaining his character, he pointed out that despite being an action-driven film
, Half
does not feature a single slow-motion shot, reflecting the team's intention to create a distinctive theatrical experience.
Actress Aiswarya Raj highlighted the sibling relationship as one
of the aspects of the film that resonated most strongly with her. She acknowledged that learning and performing the action sequences was
challenging and quite different from what she had anticipated.  Describing
Half
as one of the most striking portrayals of vampires, she
said the film presents them as friendly, relatable, almost next-door characters rather than conventional supernatural beings.
Producer Anne Sanjeev spoke about the film's bold concept and distinctive theme, emphasising the team's ambition to take Malayalam cinema beyond geographical boundaries. The team, she added, was keen to introduce its distinctive story to international audiences. She also expressed her hope of bringing more unique and engaging content to viewers in the future.

title: Saurabh Sachdeva Urges Aspiring Actors to Overcome Fear, Embrace Risks and Align Actions with Ambitions at IFFI Masterclass
content:
Goa, 24 November 2026
A masterclass titled ‘
What Stops You from Being an Actor
’, conducted by actor and acting coach Shri Saurabh Sachdeva, was held today at Kala Academy, Goa, as part of the 57th International Film Festival of India (IFFI). The session witnessed the participation of numerous young acting enthusiasts and explored the psychological, practical and personal barriers that often prevent aspiring actors from pursuing their ambitions.
Through interactive discussions and practical examples, Shri Sachdeva encouraged participants to look beyond the desire to become actors and examine the fears, habits and attitudes that may be holding them back.
Addressing the uncertainty surrounding auditions and rejection, he explained that actors may not always know why they are selected or rejected, as casting decisions often involve several people. Advising participants not to become emotionally attached to individual auditions, he said, “
You will never know. The only thing you can do is you can ask them how it felt, that's all
.” He further emphasised the importance of accepting the outcome, continuing to audition and moving forward rather than waiting indefinitely for a response.
A central theme of the masterclass was the distinction between liking something and genuinely caring about it. Challenging participants to reflect on their commitment, Sachdeva asked, “
Do you like to be an actor or do you care to be an actor
?” He explained that while liking something may remain at the level of interest, caring requires responsibility, attention and consistent effort. “Most of us like our work, we don't care about our work,” he observed, urging aspiring actors to assess whether their actions demonstrate the commitment needed to pursue their dreams.
Addressing the fear of social judgement, he identified social risk as another significant barrier. “The major problem is social risk,” he observed, explaining that acting requires individuals to expose themselves to scrutiny, approach people and communicate without being overly concerned about how others perceive them. He emphasised that performers must develop the confidence to express themselves and engage with people.
Emphasising the need to align ambition with action, Sachdeva encouraged participants to examine whether their daily routines and habits reflected the level
of achievement they hoped to attain. He explained that different levels of ambition require corresponding levels of preparation, discipline and commitment, including changes in training, physical preparation, lifestyle and everyday habits.
Reflecting on the importance of purpose, Sachdeva asked participants to revisit the reasons that first inspired them to pursue acting, noting that one's motivation can evolve with personal experiences. Sharing his own journey, he spoke about how his initial struggles with self-expression shaped his purpose. Describing it as
“to give expression to people and give power to create
,” he encouraged aspiring performers to remain connected to their ‘why’ and focus on self-expression through their art, rather than measuring their journey solely through auditions, selection or external recognition.
The masterclass encouraged participants to look inward and reconsider what pursuing acting truly demands. Through his insights, Sachdeva emphasised that moving beyond fear, accepting rejection, taking risks, strengthening fundamentals and translating ambition into consistent action are essential not only to becoming an actor but also to sustaining a meaningful journey in the performing arts.

title: From Everyday Life to the Supernatural: Director Akhil Sathyan on the Making of Sarvam Maya at 57th IFFI
subtitle: “Humour Can Be as Powerful as Drama and Thrill in Cinema”: Akhil Sathyan
content:
Goa, 24 November 2026
Drawing inspiration from everyday encounters and deeply personal experiences, Malayalam filmmaker Shri Akhil Sathyan spoke about the making of his supernatural drama
Sarvam Maya
at a press conference during the 57th International Film Festival of India (IFFI) in Goa today. The 2025 Malayalam-language feature, starring Nivin Pauly and Riya Shibu, is being screened in the
Indian Panorama
section of IFFI 2026.
Describing
Sarvam Maya
as a deeply personal film with a homegrown sensibility, Shri Akhil recalled that both he and his friend Nivin Pauly were apprehensive about making a horror film, given their own fear of the genre
. The idea took shape following an encounter at a temple with a priest who had previously been an atheist.
This everyday experience inspired the unconventional premise of an atheist priest who performs exorcisms and finds himself in the company of a Gen Z ghost.
Written and directed by Shri Akhil Sathyan,
Sarvam Maya
follows Prabhendu, a musician and atheist who is compelled by family circumstances to become a traditional Hindu priest. His life takes an unexpected turn when he encounters Maya, also known as ‘Delulu’, the spirit of a young woman struggling to come to terms with her past. Their unlikely friendship becomes a journey of self-discovery, exploring faith, loss, love and the healing power of human connection.
Speaking about the role of humour in his storytelling, Shri Akhil Sathyan emphasised that a film need not rely on violence or action sequences that do not serve its narrative to engage audiences. Humour, he observed, could contribute to a film’s commercial appeal just as effectively as drama or thrill, while also lending beauty and emotional depth to a story. He added that Nivin Pauly’s natural sense of humour made their collaboration particularly enjoyable.
Expressing happiness about the selection of the film, while he had initially been uncertain about submitting a film that had already enjoyed a commercial run, he believed, its emotional resonance and narrative depth could find appreciation at the festival.
Asked about the influence of his father and veteran filmmaker Shri Sathyan Anthikad, Shri Akhil said the distinctly local elements in his films emerged naturally from his own experiences. While he was initially drawn to the cinema of Shri Mani Ratnam, particularly films such as
Bombay
, he gradually developed a deeper appreciation of his father’s works, including
Varavelpu
. He also acknowledged the influence of veteran actor and screenwriter Shri Sreenivasan.
Having moved from a career in information technology to filmmaking, Shri Akhil Sathyan encouraged aspiring filmmakers, particularly those without an industry background, to begin with writing a compelling idea for a two-minute film and then shooting and editing it. A pencil and paper, he said, could be enough to take the first step into cinema, and a well-written idea could change the course of one’s future.
Through the unlikely friendship between an atheist priest and a young spirit,
Sarvam Maya
brings together humour, tenderness and reflections on faith and loss. In keeping with IFFI 2026’s theme, ‘Stories Without Borders’, the film reflects the ability of stories rooted in local experiences to connect with audiences through universal human emotions.
The press conference was moderated by Shri Alan Siby.

title: Her Lens, Her Legacy, Her Liberty: Women Filmmakers on Redefining Narratives in World Cinema at 57th IFFI
content:
Goa,24 November, 2026
Women filmmakers from diverse cultural backgrounds shared their experiences and perspectives on identity, cultural heritage and creative freedom at a panel discussion titled
‘Her Lens, Her Legacy, Her Liberty: Women Shaping World Cinema’
, held on the sidelines of the 57th International Film Festival of India (IFFI) in Goa
. The session featured Kyrgyz writer-director Narghiza Dotieva, Romanian-Roma actress and filmmaker Alina Șerban, and Mexican-American
writer-director Suzanne Andrews Correa. Indian filmmaker Abhishek Jain moderated the discussion.
Opening the discussion, Jain invited the panellists to reflect on their personal journeys and the cultural influences that shaped their cinematic voices. Narghiza Dotieva, who was born in Kyrgyzstan and grew up in a small lakeside fishing town, recalled how her grandfather’s recitations of traditional Kyrgyz oral poetry inspired her love for storytelling. After a career in advertising, she self-funded her early filmmaking projects, drawing inspiration from Kyrgyzstan’s literary and cultural heritage, including the epic
Manas
. Her feature debut,
Skylark
, explores borderland histories and universal human emotions.
Born into a Roma family in Bucharest, Romania, Alina Șerban, described her participation at IFFI as an emotional return to her ancestral homeland. She noted the historical links between the Roma
community and Rajasthan, including the presence of words of Indian origin in the Roma language. Having experienced prejudice and social marginalisation while growing up in Bucharest, Șerban turned to theatre and cinema to challenge stereotypes. Through
her work, including her feature directorial venture
I Matter
, she seeks to reclaim agency over Roma narratives and foreground stories of resilience and dignity.
Mexican-American filmmaker Suzanne Andrews Correa spoke about the decade-long journey behind her feature directorial debut,
La Cazadora (The Huntress)
, set in Ciudad Juárez, Mexico. Inspired by real-life incidents of feminicide and violence against women, the film evolved from an expression of anger and urgency into an empathetic exploration of desperation, survival and female agency.
The panellists also discussed the structural challenges facing independent filmmakers, including funding constraints, gender bias and stereotyping. Correa observed that producers often hesitate to support complex and uncomfortable subjects in favour of commercially safer narratives, while women directors frequently have to prove their credentials to be taken seriously. Șerban recounted facing repeated funding rejections because her scripts did not conform to stereotypical portrayals of the Roma community. Both emphasised the importance of being recognised for artistic merit rather than token representation. Dotieva added that audiences and film festivals have an important role in supporting diverse, culturally rooted stories from underrepresented regions.
Drawing on their own creative journeys, the panelists encouraged aspiring filmmakers to remain true to their emotional and cultural roots, observing that deeply authentic local stories can resonate with audiences across the world.

title: ‘Awtar Kaul: The (In)Complete Story’ Revisits the Life and Cinematic Legacy of Filmmaker Awtar Kaul
subtitle: Author Vinod Kaul shares insights into Awtar Kaul’s life, his film ‘27 Down’ and his unfinished creative journey during an interaction at the 57th IFFI
content:
Goa, 24 November 2026
Indian cinema has seen filmmakers whose creative journeys ended too soon, but whose work continues to hold significance. Awtar Kaul was one such filmmaker. His only feature film,
27 Down
(1974), is regarded as an important work of Indian cinema.
The life and cinematic legacy of Awtar Kaul are explored in the book
Awtar Kaul: The (In)Complete Story
, published by the Publications Division. Authored by Vinod Kaul, the book brings together letters, photographs, personal memories and conversations to document the filmmaker’s life and creative journey. The book was released on November 21, 2026, during the 57th International Film Festival of India (IFFI) in Goa.
During an interaction at IFFI on November 23, author Vinod Kaul spoke about the inspiration behind the book and his efforts to bring Awtar Kaul’s story to a wider audience. He shared that the idea did not begin with a plan to write a book on a filmmaker. It began as a personal effort to know more about his uncle, who passed away when Vinod Kaul was in Class Two.
He recalled how he began collecting his uncle’s photographs, letters and other documents. Over time, this personal search developed into a deeper effort to understand Awtar Kaul’s life and contribution to Indian cinema.
Vinod Kaul said that as he grew older, he realised the importance of
27 Down
. He often wondered why a filmmaker of such talent, who had made such a remarkable film, was not widely known. This encouraged him to research Awtar Kaul’s life and introduce his story to a new generation and future filmmakers.
Explaining the title
The (In)Complete Story
, Vinod Kaul said that very little had been written about Awtar Kaul and his work. The book attempts to bring his story together, making it complete in one sense. However, his life and creative journey remained incomplete. He had a short married life and made only one film. The author observed that had Awtar Kaul lived longer, he might have made many more films.
Sharing an emotional experience from his research, Vinod Kaul spoke about discovering that his aunt, Ann Kaul, who was from America, had also passed away. The family had not known about her death. He described the discovery as a major shock and said that the research brought several unexpected and emotional experiences to light.
Speaking about the relationship between cinema and literature, Vinod Kaul said that the two have always been closely connected, with many films drawing inspiration from novels, stories and other literary works. He appreciated the Publications Division for its efforts to highlight this relationship and bring the stories of filmmakers and works connected with cinema to readers. He also expressed gratitude to the Division for providing a platform to bring Awtar Kaul’s story to a wider audience.
On what young filmmakers can learn from Awtar Kaul, Vinod Kaul said that they should remain committed to their creative choices. At a time when mainstream films such as
Zanjeer
,
Bobby
and
Yaadon Ki Baaraat
were popular, Awtar Kaul chose to follow his own interests and make an art film. Vinod Kaul encouraged young filmmakers to study the storytelling, craft, message and filmmaking style of
27 Down
.
Preserving a Cinematic Legacy
Awtar Kaul: The (In)Complete Story is not merely a record of a filmmaker’s life; it is also an effort to reconnect personal memories with an important chapter in Indian cinema. What began as a nephew’s search to understand his uncle has evolved into an attempt to bring Awtar Kaul’s life and contribution back into public memory.
Through this publication, the Publications Division seeks to document the contributions of filmmakers like Awtar Kaul and introduce their creative legacy to a new generation of readers, students and cinema enthusiasts.

title: Prasar Bharati Announces Winners of First-Ever Script Pitching Lab ‘Page Se Pitch Tak’ at IFFI 2026
subtitle: Avishesh Jha Wins First Prize for ‘Mirchi Cake’; Satya Vyas and Jitesh Thakur Secure Second and Third Prizes
content:
Goa, 24 November 2026
Prasar Bharati today announced the winners of its inaugural
Script Pitching Lab, ‘Page Se Pitch Tak’,
at Kala Academy, Panaji, as part of the 57th International Film Festival of India (IFFI). Conceived by Prasar Bharati Chairman Shri Prasoon Joshi, the initiative aims to establish an annual national platform for emerging writers to showcase original stories in ten Indian languages across the categories of feature films, documentaries and short films.
The initiative received an overwhelming response, with nearly 1,000 scripts submitted within just ten days of the announcement, reflecting the immense storytelling talent and creative aspirations of young writers across the country.
Avishesh Jha emerged as the first-prize winner for his script ‘Mirchi Cake’, receiving a cash award of ₹5 lakh. Satya Vyas secured the second prize for ‘संहार’, winning ₹3 lakh, while Jitesh Thakur won the third prize for ‘Sharad Poornima’, receiving ₹2 lakh.
The awards were presented at a ceremony attended by Shri Prithul Kumar, Joint Secretary, Ministry of Information and Broadcasting, and Shri Dhiraj Singh, Managing Director, National Film Development Corporation (NFDC).
Addressing the gathering, Shri Prithul Kumar emphasised the importance of identifying and nurturing emerging storytelling talent. He said that it was essential to tap into the creative potential of young India and discover the stories that the country’s youth aspire to tell. Highlighting the significance of scripting in filmmaking, he observed that putting a script together was the first step in the filmmaking process, with planning being fundamental to making a film. Describing the script as synonymous with planning, he stressed that a compelling script and a strong story formed the foundation of successful filmmaking,
Ms. Rina Sonowal Kouli, Director General, Doordarshan, delivered the welcome address, highlighting the significance of the initiative in bringing India's linguistic and creative diversity to the forefront. She underscored the importance of creating opportunities for emerging writers to showcase their original ideas on a national platform.
The pitching sessions featured ten shortlisted participants presenting their original scripts before an eminent jury comprising Shri Manoj Joshi, actor and National Film Award winner for Best Supporting Actor; Shri Sandeep Balakrishna; author, editor and independent researcher in Indian history, culture and literature; Shri Shree Narayan Singh, filmmaker and editor known for films such as ‘Toilet: Ek Prem Katha’ and ‘Batti Gul Meter Chalu’; and Shri Anant Vijay, National Film Award-winning journalist, author and film critic, and Vice-Chairman of the Governing Council of the Film and Television Institute of India (FTII), Pune.
Recognising excellence across the shortlisted entries, the initiative also presented special mention awards of ₹50,000 each to participants securing the fourth, fifth and sixth positions. Certificates of appreciation were awarded to those securing the seventh, eighth, ninth and tenth positions, while participation certificates were presented to the best 30 shortlisted writers.
Held from 21st to 23rd November, 2026, ‘Page Se Pitch Tak’ seeks to bridge the gap between emerging writers and the film industry by providing a platform for original ideas to find their way to the screen. Envisioned as an annual initiative, it aims to connect promising storytellers with industry professionals and create opportunities for their scripts to evolve into feature films, documentaries and short-film productions.

title: Marathi Film Aadi Anant Explores Intergenerational Bonds, Love and the Realities of Caregiving at 57th IFFI
content:
Goa, 24 November 24
Filmmaker Mahesh Limaye shared the creative journey behind his Marathi feature film Aadi Anant, screened in the Indian Panorama section, at a press conference organised by the Press Information Bureau (PIB) during the 57th International Film Festival of India (IFFI) in Goa.
The 137-minute film explores the bond between Aditya, a young actor struggling to establish himself, and his spirited grandfather Anant Rao, played by Sankarshan Karhade and renowned veteran actor Ashok Saraf, respectively. Saraf was recently honoured with the Padma Shri.
Addressing the media, Limaye explained how the story unfolds through affection, light-hearted banter and mutual support as the both characters navigate financial and personal challenges. Their relationship takes a difficult turn when an accident leaves Anant Rao bedridden, forcing Aditya to balance his caregiving responsibilities with his acting ambitions. As pressure and frustration begin to strain their bond, the film explores family responsibility, the often-overlooked realities of caregiving and the meaning of success in contemporary life.
Limaye recalled being deeply moved when actor-writer Sankarshan Karhade first narrated the script, as it brought back memories of caring for his own father during his final days. While rooted in Marathi storytelling, he said, the film’s emotional core transcends linguistic boundaries and reflects experiences shared by families across India and beyond.
Speaking about the film’s music and collaborative spirit, Limaye revealed that
Aadi Anant
features a devotional bhajan rendered by classical vocalist Rahul Deshpande, with Ashok Saraf playing the tabla on screen. He praised Saraf’s humility and dedication, noting that the veteran actor approached the layered and unfamiliar character with the openness of a newcomer. The mutual respect between Saraf and Karhade, he added, brought an effortless rhythm to their on-screen relationship.
The title
Aadi Anant
captures the contrast between ‘Aadi’, meaning beginning, and ‘Anant’, meaning timeless, reflecting the film’s exploration of relationships across generations.
An alumnus of Mumbai’s J. J. School of Art, Mahesh Limaye is a cinematographer and director. His directorial debut,
Yellow
, won three National Film Awards, while his second feature,
Jaggu Ani Juliet
, received seven Maharashtra State Film Awards.
Aadi Anant
marks his third feature film as director.
Shivraj Gangawal moderated the press conference.

title: The Black Sea Explores Universal Human Emotions Through a Distinctive Cinematic Approach at IFFI 2026
subtitle: The film examines the extremes of human desire and their consequences: Director Aladdin Mostafa
content:
Goa, 24 November 2026
The makers of the Arabic-language feature film
The Black Sea
addressed the media today at the Press Information Bureau (PIB) Media Centre during the 57th International Film Festival of India in Goa. Debutant director Aladdin Mostafa, producer Hamdy Sameh, and film editor and executive producer Motaz Nashy interacted with journalists, sharing insights into the film’s genesis, universal relevance, and deliberate editorial craft.
Speaking about the inspiration behind
The Black Sea
and choosing the subject for his maiden feature, director Aladdin Mostafa expressed his delight at presenting the film at IFFI and bringing a story from Arab culture to an international platform. Elaborating on the central theme, he stated that the film examines how unchecked human desires can spiral when individuals pursue their goals at any cost, questioning the lengths to which people go when they resort to extreme actions to fulfil their ambitions.
Responding to a question on bringing an Egyptian film to Indian and global audiences at the festival, producer Hamdy Sameh highlighted the story's cross-cultural resonance. He noted that although
The Black Sea
is an Egyptian production in the Arabic language, it is not restricted to any specific culture or geography. “It speaks to something shared by people across nations. Human beings everywhere experience the same fundamental desires, which allows the film to connect with audiences in India and across the world,” he said.
Sharing perspectives on the technical and narrative approach of the film which revolves around characters confined indoors and drawn into a dark psychological app, film editor and executive producer Motaz Nashy spoke about using rhythm and pacing to convey tension and confinement. He noted that the primary challenge lay in ensuring the film’s deeper concepts were effectively communicated to all viewers. Rather than opting for rapid cuts, the team consciously adopted a slower, deliberate pace so that audiences could immerse themselves in the characters' experience and feel the core message the filmmakers set out to deliver.
The press conference concluded with the filmmakers expressing gratitude to festival organizers and Indian audiences for their warm reception. With its atmospheric pacing and thought-provoking premise,
The Black Sea
offers viewers at IFFI 57 an immersive cinematic experience that bridges regional storytelling with global human truths. The Press Conference was moderated by Ms. Shrushti Suresh Kulye.
Rooted in Egyptian culture yet exploring themes that resonate across societies,
The Black Sea
reflects the spirit of IFFI 2026’s theme, ‘Stories Without Borders’. Through its universal exploration of human desires and its distinctive approach to storytelling, the film illustrates how cinema transcends linguistic and cultural boundaries, bringing audiences together through shared human experiences.

title: Dr. Ambedkar Foundation to Organise Constitution Day Celebration on 26 November Thursday
subtitle:
Union Minister Dr. Virendra Kumar to Grace the Occasion as Chief Guest; Ministers of State for Social Justice & Empowerment, Shri Ramdas Athawale and Shri B.L. Verma To Grace The Occasion

Former Chief Justice of India Justice U.U. Lalit to Deliver Constitution Day Lecture on “Constitutional Governance and the Legacy of Dr. B.R. Ambedkar”
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                24 NOV 2026 8:10PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Dr. Ambedkar Foundation (DAF), under the Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment, Government of India,
is organising the
Constitution Day Celebration at Dr. Ambedkar International Centre (DAIC), on November 26, Thursday in the National Capital, here.
The programme will commemorate the adoption of the Constitution of India on November 26, 1949, and reaffirm the enduring contribution of Bharat Ratna Dr. B.R. Ambedkar, Chairman of the Drafting Committee of the Constituent Assembly, in shaping the constitutional and democratic foundations of the nation.
The celebration will be organised on the theme
“The Constitution @76: Dr. B.R. Ambedkar's Constitutional Vision and the Future of Indian Democracy”.
The theme underscores the continuing relevance of the constitutional ideals of justice, liberty, equality and fraternity and seeks to foster deeper engagement with Dr. Ambedkar's vision of constitutional morality, democratic governance, institutional accountability and an inclusive society. It will also provide a platform for deliberations on the role of constitutional values in addressing contemporary challenges and strengthening India's democratic framework.
Dr. Virendra Kumar, Hon'ble Union Minister for Social Justice & Empowerment and Chairman, Dr. Ambedkar Foundation,
will grace the occasion as the Chief Guest.
Shri Ramdas Athawale and Shri B.L. Verma, Hon'ble Ministers of State for Social Justice & Empowerment,
will also address the gathering. Shri Sudhansh Pant, Secretary, Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment, will also participate in the programme.
A key highlight of the celebration will be the reading of the Preamble to the Constitution by
Hon'ble Mr. Justice Uday Umesh Lalit, Former Chief Justice of India.
Justice Lalit will also deliver the Constitution Day Lecture on the subject
“Constitutional Governance and the Legacy of Dr. B.R. Ambedkar”.
His address will reflect upon the foundational principles of the Indian Constitution, Dr. Ambedkar's contribution to the evolution of India's constitutional democracy and the continuing significance of his ideas in strengthening democratic institutions and ensuring social justice.
The programme will bring together Chair Professors, Assistant Professors and Doctoral Fellows associated with Dr. Ambedkar Chairs established in universities across the country, along with eminent academicians, researchers, scholars, senior government officials and other distinguished invitees. An academic interaction will also be organised as part of the celebration, providing a forum for meaningful exchange of perspectives on constitutional values, social transformation, social justice and the future of Indian democracy.
The participation of scholars and academic representatives associated with Dr. Ambedkar Chairs will further strengthen the academic discourse on his philosophy, intellectual legacy and contribution to nation-building. The interaction will also encourage the dissemination of Ambedkarite thought and promote greater awareness of the Constitution among academic institutions and the wider public.
The Constitution of India, adopted by the Constituent Assembly on November 26, 1949, and brought into force on January 26, 1950, embodies the collective aspirations of the people of India and establishes the framework for a sovereign, socialist, secular and democratic republic. Constitution Day, also known as
Samvidhan Diwas
, is observed annually on November 26 to commemorate the adoption of the Constitution and promote awareness of its values and principles.
Through this celebration, the Dr. Ambedkar Foundation seeks to further strengthen public understanding of the Constitution and reaffirm its commitment to disseminating the thoughts, philosophy and ideals of Dr. B.R. Ambedkar. The initiative also aims to encourage dialogue on constitutional democracy, equality, dignity, fraternity and social inclusion, reinforcing the vision of an equitable, empowered and inclusive India.

title: Union Minister Dr Virendra Kumar Visits Siddharth Nasha Mukti Kendra in Lucknow
subtitle:
Minister Interacts with Beneficiaries, Reviews Treatment and Rehabilitation Facilities; Directs Centre Management to Strengthen Infrastructure, Hygiene and Counselling Services

De-Addiction centres function not merely as treatment facilities but as comprehensive rehabilitation spaces supporting physical, psychological, emotional and social reintegration of beneficiaries: Dr Virendra Kumar
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                24 NOV 2026 6:26PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Union Minister for Social Justice and Empowerment, Dr. Virendra Kumar, today visited
Siddharth Nasha Mukti Kendra
, at Thakurganj, in Lucknow, Uttar Pradesh, to review the functioning of the de-addiction and rehabilitation facility and assess the quality of services being provided to persons undergoing treatment for substance dependence.
The Centre, is run by the voluntary organisation
Bhartiya Samaj Seva Sansthan, Lucknow
.
During the visit, the Minister was informed about the ongoing activities, services provided, treatment and rehabilitation of the victims of substance abuse, at the Centre.
As part of the inspection, Dr. Virendra Kumar undertook a detailed review of the available facilities and interacted directly with the beneficiaries to understand their well-being, treatment experience and the support being provided to them. He enquired about the quality of medical care, counselling sessions and recreational facilities available at the centre.
Emphasising the importance of a comprehensive and compassionate approach to de-addiction, the Minister directed the management to further strengthen the quality, effectiveness and regularity of treatment, counselling and rehabilitation services.
Observing that the centre had been functioning from the same building for several years, the Minister directed the management to undertake necessary improvements in its infrastructure and overall appearance. He specifically instructed the authorities to ensure fresh painting of the premises and upgradation of furniture so that beneficiaries could be provided with a clean, comfortable and conducive environment during their treatment and recovery.
The Minister also inspected the cleanliness arrangements and kitchen facilities at the centre. While expressing satisfaction with the overall maintenance and kitchen arrangements, he emphasised that hygiene and sanitation must be maintained consistently. He directed the staff to sustain the existing standards and undertake further improvements wherever necessary, particularly in areas related to food preparation, cleanliness and the daily living environment of beneficiaries.
Highlighting the importance of emotional, mental and spiritual well-being in the process of recovery from substance dependence, Dr. Virendra Kumar directed the centre management to earmark a dedicated and peaceful space within the premises for daily prayers and worship.
He further advised the management to periodically invite representatives of reputed spiritual and humanitarian organisations, including The Art of Living, Brahma Kumaris and other such institutions, to conduct positive counselling and motivational sessions for the beneficiaries. Such engagements, he emphasised, could complement medical treatment and psychological counselling by fostering positivity, self-confidence, inner strength and a sense of purpose among individuals undergoing rehabilitation.
The Minister underscored the need to ensure that de-addiction centres function not merely as treatment facilities but as comprehensive rehabilitation spaces that support the physical, psychological, emotional and social reintegration of beneficiaries.
The Union Minister’s visit reflects the emphasis of Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment on strengthening the monitoring of de-addiction and rehabilitation facilities, ensuring quality service delivery and promoting a beneficiary-centric approach to drug demand reduction. The directions issued by the Minister are intended to further improve the standards of care, infrastructure and rehabilitation support at the centre, with an emphasis on their time-bound implementation.
Officials from the Prohibition Department and the State Social Welfare Department, the Centre Director, Shri Jitendra Verma, along with other staff members, were present on the occasion.
